title: Diet and Obesity presentation
subject: listening

paragraphs.text: ADAM: OK Rosie, shall we try to get some ideas together for our presentation on diet and obesity?
ROSIE: Sure.
ADAM: I can talk about the experiment I did to see if people can tell the difference between real sugar and artificial sweeteners.
ROSIE: Where you gave people drinks with either sugar or artificial sweeteners and they had to say which they thought it was?

ADAM: Yeah. It took me ages to decide exactly how I’d organise it, especially how I could make sure that people didn’t know which drink I was giving them. It was hard to keep track of it all, especially as I had so many people doing it – I had to make sure I kept a proper record of what each person had had.
ROSIE: So could most people tell the difference?
ADAM: Yeah – I hadn’t thought they would be able to, but most people could.
ROSIE: Then there’s that experiment I did measuring the fat content of nuts, to see if the nutritional information given on the packet was accurate.
ADAM: The one where you ground up the nuts and mixed them with a chemical to absorb the fat?

ROSIE: Yes. My results were a bit problematic – the fat content for that type of nut seemed much lower than it said on the package. But I reckon the package information was right. I think I should probably have ground up the nuts more than I did. It’s possible that the scales for weighing the fat weren’t accurate enough, too. I’d really like to try the experiment again some time.

ADAM: So what can we say about helping people to lose weight? There’s a lot we could say about what restaurants could do to reduce obesity. I read that the items at the start of a menu and the items at the end of a menu are much more likely to be chosen than the items in the middle. So, if you put the low-calorie items at the beginning and end of the menu, people will probably go for the food with fewer calories, without even realising what they’re doing.
ROSIE: I think food manufacturers could do more to encourage healthy eating.
ADAM: How?

ROSIE: Well, when manufacturers put calorie counts of a food on the label, they’re sometimes really confusing and I suspect they do it on purpose. Because food that’s high in calories tastes better, and so they’ll sell more.
ADAM: Yeah, so if you look at the amount of calories in a pizza, they’ll give you the calories per quarter pizza and you think, oh that’s not too bad. But who’s going to eat a quarter pizza?
ROSIE: Exactly.
ADAM: I suppose another approach to this problem is to get people to exercise more.

ROSIE: Right. In England, the current guidelines are for at least 30 minutes of brisk walking, five days a week. Now when you ask them, about 40% of men and 30% of women say they do this, but when you objectively measure the amount of walking they do with motion sensors, you find that only 6% of men and 4% of women do the recommended amount of exercise.
ADAM: Mm, so you can see why obesity is growing.
ROSIE: So how can people be encouraged to take more exercise?

ADAM: Well, for example, think of the location of stairs in a train station. If people reach the stairs before they reach the escalator when they’re leaving the station, they’re more likely to take the stairs. And if you increase the width of the stairs, you’ll get more people using them at the same time. It’s an unconscious process and influenced by minor modifications in their environment.
ROSIE: Right. And it might not be a big change, but if it happens every day, it all adds up.
ADAM: Yes. But actually, I’m not sure if we should be talking about exercise in our presentation.
ROSIE: Well, we’ve done quite a bit of reading about it.
ADAM: I know, but it’s going to mean we have a very wide focus, and our tutor did say that we need to focus on causes and solutions in terms of nutrition.
ROSIE: I suppose so. And we’ve got plenty of information about that. OK, well that will be simpler.
ADAM: So what shall we do now? We’ve still got half an hour before our next lecture.
ROSIE: Let’s think about what we’re going to include and what will go where. Then we can decide what slides we need.
ADAM: OK, fine.

Questions 21 and 22

Choose TWO letters, A–E.

questions.prompt: Which TWO points does Adam make about his experiment on artificial sweeteners?

options.text: The results were what he had predicted.
The experiment was simple to set up.
A large sample of people was tested.
The subjects were unaware of what they were drinking.
The test was repeated several times for each person.

options.text: She used the wrong sort of nuts.

groups.instruction:
Questions 25–30

Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

questions.prompt: Adam suggests that restaurants could reduce obesity if their menus

options.text: offered fewer options.
had more low-calorie foods.
were organised in a particular way.

questions.explanation: 25. 通过题干关键词restaurant、reduce obesity、menus定位到原文中的核心信息，文中的put the low-calorie items at the beginning and the end of the menu对应选项C中的organised in a particular way，此题为直叙。

questions.prompt: The students agree that food manufacturers deliberately

options.text: make calorie counts hard to understand.
fail to provide accurate calorie counts.
use ineffective methods to reduce calories.

questions.explanation: 26. 题干定位词food manufacturer原文重现，deliberately和原文中的on purpose是同义替换，意思是“故意地”。原文中的confusing对应选项A的hard to understand，题目答案先出现，定位词的同义替换on purpose 后出现。

questions.prompt: What does Rosie say about levels of exercise in England?

options.text: The amount recommended is much too low.
Most people overestimate how much they do.
Women now exercise more than they used to.

questions.explanation: 27. 题干定位词England和levels of exercise在原文中比较稳定，能帮助定位。在提到exercise和England之后，原文中出现了关于运动的数据，40%的男性和30%的女性表示达到了官方推荐的运动时间，而通过motion sensor运动传感器测到的数据，只有6%的男性和4%的女性真正达到了推荐的运动时长，与选项B中的overestimate（高估）意思相符。

questions.prompt: Adam refers to the location and width of stairs in a train station to illustrate

options.text: practical changes that can influence people’s behaviour.
methods of helping people who have mobility problems.
ways of preventing accidents by controlling crowd movement.

questions.explanation: 28. 题干定位词train station是专有名词词组，比较稳定，可以帮助定位，题目核心词location和width of stairs进一步帮助确定答案句。原文中提到如果改变楼梯的位置和宽度会有更多人走楼梯，和选项A意思相符。

questions.prompt: What do the students agree about including reference to exercise in their presentation?

options.text: They should probably leave it out.
They need to do more research on it.
They should discuss this with their tutor.

questions.explanation: 29. 题干定位词exercise帮助定位到原文相关信息，I’m not sure if...后面讲到tutor要求他专注于跟营养有关的信息，所以不需要和exercise相关的信息。选项A 中leave out表示“省去”，和原文相符。本题的难点在于，答案相关信息分散在不同的句子里，考生需要根据上下文去推测和整合信息，才能找到答案。

questions.prompt: What are the students going to do next for their presentation?

options.text: prepare some slides for it
find out how long they have for it
decide on its content and organisation

questions.explanation: 30. 本题答案为直叙。选项C中的its content对应原文中的what we’re going to include，organisation对应原文中的what will go where。
